title: Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular
summary: Every abelian surface and every genus two curve over a totally real field is potentially automorphic and satisfies the Hasse–Weil conjecture (Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni). The roadmap plans the GSp_4 modularity lifting theorem for ordinary parallel weight 2 representations — Taylor–Wiles patching in defect 0 and 1 on higher Hida complexes, doubling, analytic continuation and étale descent — and its consequences: potential modularity by a p–q switch, potential automorphy, modularity of ordinary surfaces, surfaces with fixed 3-torsion and the paramodular conjecture.
readme:
**Purpose.** Boxer, Calegari, Gee and Pilloni prove that every abelian surface and every genus two curve over a totally real field is potentially automorphic, hence satisfies the Hasse–Weil conjecture; that challenging abelian surfaces (End_C A = Z, or type B[C_2]) are potentially modular; that genus one curves over arbitrary quadratic extensions of totally real fields are potentially modular; and that there are infinitely many modular abelian surfaces over Q with End_C A = Z. This roadmap plans the argument from the modularity lifting theorem onwards and the paper's final theorems.

**Scope.** Layers AP.0–AP.7 plan: the GSp_4 conventions for abelian surfaces and the notions of automorphy and modularity; the Galois representations of ordinary parallel weight 2 forms; the Taylor–Wiles set-up, Galois representations on Hida–Hecke algebras and patching in defect 0 and 1 (BCGP §§7.7–7.11); Ihara avoidance and multiplicities (§§7.12–7.13); gluing by étale descent and the lifting theorems (§8); potential modularity and automorphy (§9); and the modularity applications and the paramodular conjecture (§10).

**Conventions.** F is totally real and p ≥ 3 splits completely in F. ε is the p-adic cyclotomic character, ν the similitude character of GSp_4, rec_{GT,p} Gan–Takeda's local Langlands correspondence normalized as in BCGP §2.3; Galois representations of abelian surfaces are H^1 (geometric Frobenius), GSp_4-valued with multiplier ε^{−1}. Forms are of parallel weight 2 with central character |·|^2 unless stated. Everything that uses Arthur's classification for GSp_4 carries its conditional status as recorded at ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.0 and ML.4.

**Boundaries.** Imported, never planned here: Hilbert–Siegel varieties, their integral models, compactifications and strata (Hilbert–Siegel Part II of HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves); higher Hida and higher Coleman theory, including the doubling theorem (HigherHidaAndColemanTheory); integral coherent cohomology with its Hecke action and the Taylor–Wiles descent statement (Part II of AutomorphicBundles); GSp_4 local representation theory, its Galois representations in regular weight and its functorial transfers (GSp_4 Part II of ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions); local and global GSp_4 deformation rings and residual-image conditions (LocalGaloisDeformationRings, GlobalGaloisDeformations, ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations); patching algebra (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra); Moret-Bailly and rank 2 potential modularity (PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems, ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.2); open image theorems (Part II of FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems). Owned here and imported by GSp4NonregularModularityLifting and AbelianSurfacesModularity: the Galois representations of ordinary parallel weight 2 forms (BCGP25 Theorem 1.8.17), the twisted Siegel moduli, the odd-theta cover P(ρ̄), the local seed curves at 3 (BCGP25 Corollary 9.3.6 and Lemma 9.3.7), Lemma 10.3.1 and the paramodular conjecture.

**Sources.** Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular, Publ. Math. IHÉS 134 (2021), arXiv:1812.09269v3; Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni, Modularity theorems for abelian surfaces, arXiv:2502.20645v1, for Theorem 1.8.17 and §§8.1, 9.2–9.3.

**Layer overview.** AP.0 statements and weight 2 Galois representations → AP.1 Taylor–Wiles set-up → AP.2 Galois representations on Hida–Hecke algebras → AP.3 patching → AP.4 multiplicities → AP.5 gluing and the lifting theorem (Theorem 8.4.1) → AP.6 potential modularity and automorphy (Theorems 9.2.8, 9.3.1) → AP.7 modularity results and the paramodular conjecture.

**Non-goals.** §1.4.2 explains why the method stops at genus two (the weights of automorphic vector bundles occur with multiplicity at most 2); it is exposition, as are §1.2's description of the defect and §9.4's discussion of F-abelian varieties and K3 surfaces of large Picard rank.

**Proof obligations.** The design is partial: defect-one O-flatness must be proved before passage to the flat deformation-ring quotient; the p–q switch must reconcile the arbitrary prime-to-pq polarization with its chosen moduli space; and the explicit quaternionic examples need reproducible arithmetic certificates. All later targets retain these dependencies. Distinct characteristic-zero ordinary unit roots in the 2025 local seeds do not imply the residual distinctness used by the 2018 lifting theorem.

stages.title: Abelian surfaces, automorphy and weight 2 Galois representations
stages.description: Fix the conventions and the statements the rest of the roadmap proves. For an abelian surface A over a number field F, the GSp_4-valued compatible system 𝓡_A = (H^1_ét(A_{F̄}, Q̄_l))_l with multiplier ε^{−1} (BCGP Definition 2.8.2, Remark 2.8.3). Automorphy of a strictly compatible system over a number field through an isobaric sum of C-algebraic cuspidal representations matching Weil–Deligne representations at every finite place, with the completed L-function and its functional equation (Definition 9.1.1, (9.1.5)); automorphic and potentially automorphic abelian varieties (Definition 9.1.6, Remark 9.1.7); modular and potentially modular GSp_4-representations and abelian surfaces over a totally real field, with the corrected Weil–Deligne condition (Definition 9.1.8, Remark 9.1.9). The Galois representation of an ordinary cuspidal representation of GSp_4 of parallel weight 2 and central character |·|^2 over a totally real field in which p splits, with multiplier ε^{−1}, semisimplified local–global compatibility away from p and the ordinary shape at p (Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Pilloni 2025, Theorem 1.8.17), proved by interpolation over the higher Coleman eigenvariety.

stages.title: The Taylor–Wiles set-up for GSp_4 over a totally real field
stages.description: For F totally real, p ≥ 3 split in F and ρ̄: G_F → GSp_4(k) absolutely irreducible: the standing hypotheses (vast and tidy image, p-distinguished weight 2 ordinary at p, Ihara-avoidance places R with q_v ≡ 1 mod p, mod 9 if p = 3) and the auxiliary place v_0 (Hypotheses 7.7.1, 7.8.1); the global deformation problems S_χ^{I,𝔠} and S_{χ,Q}^{I,𝔠} for I ⊆ S_p over the weight algebras Λ_I (§7.7); the tame levels K^p, K_0^p(Q), K_1^p(Q), K_0^p(Q,R) and their neatness (Definition 7.8.2, Lemma 7.8.3); weights of Λ_I, classical weights, κ_2 and κ_reg (Definition 7.8.8); the Hida–Hecke modules M^{χ,I,𝔠} and M^{χ,I,𝔠,Q}, obtained by RHom^0-duality from the higher Hida complexes at these levels and localized at m̃^{I,𝔠} (7.8.4), with their Hecke algebras; Proposition 7.8.11: M^{χ,∅,𝔠,Q} is finite free over Λ_∅[Δ_Q] and, for #I = 1, M^{χ,I,𝔠,Q} is balanced over Λ_I[Δ_Q].

stages.title: Galois representations on ordinary Hida–Hecke algebras
stages.description: The doubling surjections M^{χ,I,𝔠} ⊗ Λ_{I'} → M^{χ,I',𝔠} for I ⊆ I', intertwining U_{v,1} with the chosen unit root (Proposition 7.9.1); the representation ρ^{χ,I,𝔠,Q}: G_F → GSp_4(T^{χ,I,𝔠,Q}) of type S_{χ,Q}^{I,𝔠} with Hecke-polynomial compatibility and the Klingen- and Borel-ordinary shapes above p (Theorem 7.9.4); the refined Galois representations of ordinary parallel weight 2 forms under residual hypotheses, with the base-change step of the proof repaired (Corollary 7.9.6); the descent (M^{χ,I,𝔠,Q})_{Δ_Q} ≅ M^{χ,I,𝔠} (Proposition 7.9.8).

stages.title: Patching in defect zero and one
stages.description: For #I ≤ 1: the patched ring S_∞, the patched deformation rings R_∞^{1,I,𝔠}, R_∞^{χ,I,𝔠} and modules M_∞^{1,I,𝔠}, M_∞^{χ,I,𝔠}, free in defect 0 and balanced in defect 1, obtained from the abstract patching criterion with the ideals of item 150 of the extraction, with the dimension identity dim (R_∞)' = dim S_∞ − #I (§7.11, (7.11.1)); Proposition 7.11.2: the patched modules are maximal Cohen–Macaulay over the flat quotients of the patched rings, O-flatness being proved first in defect 1. The flatness target precedes Proposition 7.11.2: in defect one its proof remains missing, so the dimension of the flat quotient cannot yet be used to bound the patched module support.

stages.title: Ihara avoidance and multiplicities
stages.description: Hypothesis 7.13.1 on a characteristic zero ρ and the levels K^{p,Iw}, K^{p,Iw_1} (Definition 7.13.4); the primes 𝔭_x and 𝔭̃^{I,𝔠}_{x'} (7.13.3), smooth points, and the eigenspaces S^{I,𝔠}_κ of p-adic forms with their duality to the patched modules; the Iwahori multiplicities d_η = 8, 4, 4, 1 of generic L-packets on the components of the Ihara-avoidance rings and d_ρ (Proposition 7.13.5); the doubling injection (Proposition 7.13.9); the regular-weight dimension counts (Proposition 7.13.11); Theorem 7.13.6: the ρ-eigenspace has dimension 8d_ρ for #I ≤ 1.

stages.title: Gluing, étale descent and the modularity lifting theorems
stages.description: Analytic continuation and étale descent of the eigenforms (Lemmas 8.2.3, 8.2.5) and the connected-component and superspecial-locus lemmas (Lemmas 8.2.7–8.2.11, Corollary 8.2.9); Theorem 8.2.1: the eigenspace has dimension 8d_ρ for every I, overconvergently; Corollary 8.2.2: ρ satisfying Hypothesis 7.13.1 is modular with full local–global compatibility; Lemma 8.3.2: solvable descent of modularity, with its general-central-character form; Theorem 8.4.1, the main modularity lifting theorem, with the unprinted hypothesis that ρ is unramified outside a finite set; Definition 8.5.1 and Theorem 8.5.2 with relaxed multiplier, its sketch written out.

stages.title: Potential modularity and potential automorphy of abelian surfaces
stages.description: Galois types of abelian surfaces and challenging surfaces (types A and B[C_2]); Proposition 9.2.1 for the others; Lemma 9.2.2 (big residual image, with the real-multiplication inert case treated separately); good primes and their density, with the strengthened choice of q (Definition 9.2.3, Lemmas 9.2.5–9.2.6); twisted Siegel moduli with fixed torsion and their local points; the fixed-determinant GL_2(F_q)-extension theorem; the corrected p–q switching Lemma 9.2.7; Theorem 9.2.8 (challenging surfaces are potentially modular); Theorem 2.7.3 (Galois representations for weight 0 GL_2 forms over a quadratic extension of a totally real field); Theorem 9.3.1 = Theorem 1.1.3 (every abelian surface over a totally real field is potentially automorphic, and Conjecture 2.8.6 holds); Corollary 9.3.3 with the corrected symmetry s ↦ 2 − s and Theorem 1.1.2 (Hasse–Weil for genus two curves and abelian surfaces); Theorem 9.3.4 = Theorem 1.1.4 (genus one curves over quadratic extensions), corrected in the CM case; Proposition 9.4.1 (Kummer surfaces). The p–q switch includes an unresolved polarization-type compatibility obligation; prime-to-pq degree alone does not put the given A in principal-polarization moduli.

stages.title: Modularity, fixed 3-torsion and the paramodular conjecture
stages.description: Proposition 10.1.1 = Theorem 1.1.7 (modularity of ordinary abelian surfaces with residually modular, vast and tidy mod p representation) and Proposition 10.1.3 (three residually modular cases), both with 'unramified' deleted; Lemmas 7.5.25–7.5.27 (crossing with dihedral extensions) and Theorem 10.1.4 (elliptic curves over quadratic extensions via mod 5); the Burkhardt quartic, the odd-theta cover P and the rationality of its twists P(ρ̄) (Definition 10.2.2, Proposition 10.2.3, Lemma 10.2.4); the local seed curves at 3 (Corollary 9.3.6 and Lemma 9.3.7 of the 2025 paper); Theorem 10.2.1 (abelian surfaces with fixed 3-torsion, ordinary clause corrected); Theorem 10.2.6 = Theorem 1.1.5 (infinitely many modular abelian surfaces with End_C = Z); Lemma 10.3.1 (the paramodular conjecture for ordinary surfaces), the original and modified paramodular conjectures (Conjecture 10.4.3), Lemma 10.3.2 (conditional), and the examples of §10.4. Local realization uses the dense Torelli open after a Kisin neighbourhood argument, including for product seeds. The scalar seeds are not residually distinguished; the explicit QM examples still require arithmetic computation certificates.
